newsitem.title: UK: Heavy moisture still threatens FSU beet crop - Licht.
newsitem.headline: Heavy moisture still threatens FSU beet crop - Licht.

text.p: Soil moisture levels remain high over sugar beet growing areas in the former Soviet Union despite last week's drier spell, leading to increased risk of damage from early frosts, statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
In its daily report, Licht said the region's beet areas stayed dry during the week ended October 8, which had helped harvesting operations, but soil wetness was still a problem.
"Crop prospects have suffered from the wetness and the harvest could run into greater problems if there should be early frosts," Licht said.
"In that case, crop expectations would have to be scaled down -- hence there remains an element of uncertainty concerning the East European crop," it added.
Russia and Ukraine are eastern Europe's two largest producers of beet sugar.
In its first estimate of world 1996/97 sugar production, released on Monday, Licht pegged Ukrainian output at 3.15 million tonnes raw value after 3.78 million in 1995/96.
Russia was expected to produce 1.82 million tonnes compared with 2.24 million a year previously, Licht said.
Total sugar production in eastern Europe would fall to 9.29 million tonnes in 1996/97 after 9.71 million in 1995/96.
